title: Investigate jstack-review nit feedback and reduce review noise
summary: ## Problem The `jstack-review` skill often surfaces **nits** that can be tedious or disproportionately time-consuming to address. In practice, I sometimes ignore them entirely, but other times they are genuinely useful. The current experience makes it difficult to tell which suggestions deserve attention. ## Investigation - Examine how `jstack-review` generates and prioritizes nit-level feedback. - Identify patterns behind low-value, repetitive, subjective, or overly pedantic suggestions versus nits that meaningfully improve maintainability or readability. - Explore how to reduce review noise **without eliminating useful observations**. - Evaluate options such as clearer severity / confidence labels, grouping minor suggestions, configurable strictness, or an easy way to defer/skip nits. - Ensure substantive correctness, security, and reliability findings remain prominent. ## Desired outcome A review experience that is actionable rather than exhausting: important findings are hard to miss, and minor suggestions are clearly optional and easy to triage. The goal is to investigate and propose an appropriate approach before committing to a particular implementation. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Document representative examples of helpful versus frustrating nits. - [ ] Propose a strategy to make nit-level feedback less disruptive. - [ ] Specify how users can still access useful nits when they want them. - [ ] Define a way to assess whether the new behavior improves review signal-to-noise ratio.
